description: From the #154 cold audit. Two client-honesty gaps that become parity gaps once \xFF/system is authoritative: (1) reads of \xFF keys are ungated anywhere - FDB bounds reads via getMaxReadKey/READ_SYSTEM_KEYS (client-side, same trust model as write gating); q67.9's client read path (GetKeyServerLocations analogue) should decide where the read bound lives. (2) A hand-crafted encoded transaction can declare read/write-conflict ranges over \xFF and conflict-abort system transactions; FDB's equivalent check is also client-side (ReadYourWrites.actor.cpp:2452-2456), so this matches the threat model but belongs on the hardening backlog - validating conflict sections at ingress would make the proxy gate complete. Neither is a corruption vector; both are foot-gun guards.

comments.text: Draft PR: https://github.com/bedrock-kv/bedrock/pull/285 — client read bound (FDB getMaxReadKey/READ_SYSTEM_KEYS) in the transaction builder, plus conflict-section validation at commit ingress with read/write bounds split per FDB getMaxRead/WriteKey. Two cold-audit rounds, both PASS-WITH-NOTES; round 1 caught that a single commit-mode bound on read conflicts made read_system_keys unusable.

title: Gate system-keyspace reads and validate conflict-range sections (FDB READ_SYSTEM_KEYS parity)
